Get ICD-10-CM release files

Source: R/get_icd10cm.R
get_icd10cm.Rd

Downloads an ICD-10-CM "code descriptions in tabular order" release from the National Center for Health Statistics (NCHS), part of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). ICD-10-CM is the US clinical modification of ICD-10, released for each US fiscal year (effective 1 October) with occasional mid-year updates.

Usage

get_icd10cm(
  dir_path = tempdir(),
  release = "latest",
  overwrite = FALSE,
  quiet = FALSE
)

Arguments

dir_path

Directory path to download to. Defaults to tempdir().

release

Character string specifying which release to download. Either:

  • "latest" (default) — the most recent release known to the package.

  • An 8-digit effective date ("YYYYMMDD"), e.g. "20261001" for the FY2027 release. See Details for the available releases.

overwrite

Logical. If TRUE, re-downloads and overwrites an existing file. Default is FALSE.

quiet

Logical. If TRUE, suppresses informational messages. Default is FALSE.

Value

File path to the downloaded release (invisibly). Depending on how NCHS published that release this is either a .zip containing the order file or the order .txt file itself; either is accepted by read_icd10cm(). The file is named icd10cm_order_<release>.<ext> so the release date can be recovered from the file name.

Details

NCHS does not name release files consistently from year to year, so the package carries a table of verified download URLs keyed by effective date. Releases known to the package (effective date, fiscal year), generated from that table when the documentation is built:

  • 20151001 (FY2016)

  • 20161001 (FY2017)

  • 20171001 (FY2018)

  • 20181001 (FY2019)

  • 20191001 (FY2020)

  • 20201001 (FY2021)

  • 20210101 (FY2021 January update)

  • 20211001 (FY2022)

  • 20220401 (FY2022 April update)

  • 20221001 (FY2023)

  • 20230401 (FY2023 April update)

  • 20231001 (FY2024)

  • 20241001 (FY2025)

  • 20251001 (FY2026)

  • 20261001 (FY2027)

Releases are keyed by their full effective date, so a fiscal year with a mid-year update has two entries (e.g. 20221001 and 20230401). The April 2024, April 2025 and April 2026 updates are deliberately absent: their code descriptions match the previous October's release, so they would give an identical code set under a second version label. A release newer than this table can be downloaded by hand from the NCHS listing and passed to read_icd10cm() or add_icd10cm() with an explicit version.

Attribution

ICD-10-CM is published by NCHS/CDC and is available free of charge at https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/icd/icd-10-cm/files.html. Use of these files does not imply endorsement by CDC, HHS or the US Government.

See also

read_icd10cm(), add_icd10cm()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
path <- get_icd10cm()
read_icd10cm(path)

# A specific release
get_icd10cm(release = "20250401")
} # }
